main_text.p: Balari Corforum lingua, Exfules dicuntur Paufaniæ: noftra Balling, & Ballartys. Apud ipfos novi orbis Indos fimilia. Illi Pagodi, Ido la dicunt: & Dei nomen agnofcis, Guatras, Flabella, quibus in argentariis excitant ignem, funt noftri Wayers. Topos, Tegmen capitis: à Top, quod verticem nobis fonat. Iam Lama, Ovu: palàm eft Lam. Sicut & Latinis adfidet Auro, Dies: etfi à fignificatione leviter abit. & Chonos, Canis, vocalibus immutatis. Si longius eam, vbi non aliqua pariatio? utiq; in Hebræis & Græcis multiplex: quod viri docti jam nuper oftenderunt. Idem in Latinis, neque negamus fexcenta effe, quæ prorfus germaniffent: fed ancipiti, ut dixi, argumento ab iis effe. Imò contrà ego certius dixerim quædam à Latinis fumpta: cùm ii imperium in noftras has oras promoverent, & fimul ad limites Germaniæ utriufq;. page.notes: Text is set in two columns of glossary entries below the running paragraph; the list is transcribed in reading order, left column first, then right column. The final entry "Boccola (item poculum" is cut off at the lower right edge; the last word is partly obscured and is read as "lum" with a superscript mark. The page is printed on a yellowed, stained paper; the dark stains at the left edge are not text. The word "Dies" and "Canis" appear in italic in the printed original; the italics above are approximate. Several glossary headwords are in italic, marked as printed. Some letters in "Pagodi" and "Guatras" are uncertain at the scan resolution.
